title: Starship Flight 14 Slips to No Earlier Than September 22
detail: NASASpaceflight reported Sept 14, 2026 that Starship Flight 14's target launch date has moved from the previously reported Sept 18 window to no earlier than Sept 22, 2026 — the third target change in as many weeks. No official reason has been disclosed, and the change does not appear to reflect a vehicle problem: Booster 21 and Ship 41 already completed their pre-launch test campaigns (B21's full-duration 33-engine static fire Aug 28; Ship 41's six-engine static fire Aug 21) and remain in final checkout at Starbase. During the gap, SpaceX moved the next-generation Ship 42 to Pad 2's launch tower on Sept 12 and exercised the chopstick arms — including lateral-translation capability and reconnecting the Ship Quick Disconnect arm — rehearsing hardware for Flight 15's planned first attempt at catching a Starship upper stage. Flight 14 itself is not planned as a catch attempt; it remains SpaceX's first bid at a full orbital insertion, carrying roughly 20 operational Starlink V3 satellites.
